sources.title: Weldbend catalog: fittings, flanges and technical data (2010 edition, current on weldbend.com)
Steel pipe specification sheets (Sch 40, 80, 160, XXH) and ASME B1.20.1 / B16.11 tolerance sheets
Pipe fittings product catalog (forged carbon steel threaded and socket weld)
Class 150 malleable iron fittings technical booklet (v4)
Knowledge base: NPT thread engagement per ASME B1.20.1; installing a gasket and flange
Standard malleable pipe fittings Class 150 (catalog section 1)
Isolation gasket installation instructions and installation checklist
Bolt reference charts for ASME B16.5 flanges
Number and size of bolts for flanged joints (ASME B16.5) and pipe schedule chart
Welded and seamless pipe dimensions and weights (hosted by Ferguson Industrial)

notes: Weights are for plain-end carbon steel pipe.
Designations shown together (Sch 40 · STD) have the same wall at that size.
tables.title: Pipe

notes: Center to end is the takeout of the fitting: from the center line to the weld end.
Long-radius 90° elbows from 22" up without catalog values are derived from the radius: A = 1.5 × NPS.
tables.title: Butt-weld elbows

notes: Concentric and eccentric reducers have the same length.
tables.title: Butt-weld reducers

notes: Lengths are for walls up to the limiting thickness in the standard; thicker walls take a longer cap. Measure it.
tables.title: Butt-weld caps

notes: Long pattern (ASME B16.9). Short-pattern stub ends (MSS SP-43) are shorter.
tables.title: Lap joint stub ends

notes: Center to bottom of socket is the takeout. Before welding, the pipe is backed off about 1/16" from the bottom of the socket.
ASME B16.11 covers socket-weld Class 3000 from 1/8" to 4", Class 6000 from 1/8" to 2" and Class 9000 from 1/2" to 2". Larger sizes vary by maker and are left out.
tables.title: Forged socket-weld fittings

notes: Center to end runs to the face of the fitting. The pipe threads in past the face, so the cut length also depends on the thread engagement.
tables.title: Forged threaded fittings

notes: Center to end runs to the face of the fitting. The pipe threads in past the face, so the cut length also depends on the thread engagement.
Class 300 isn't included yet: only one catalog prints it.
tables.title: Malleable-iron threaded fittings

notes: Wrench-tight engagement is the hand-tight engagement plus the wrench make-up (L1 + L3) for threads cut exactly to size. Thread gaging allows one turn either way on each part, so a real joint can make up a turn more or less.
tables.title: NPT pipe threads

notes: Thickness and lengths through hub run to the flange face; the raised face (1/16" on Class 150 and 300, 1/4" from Class 600) stands on top of them.
Class 900 flanges from 1/2" to 2-1/2" are made to the Class 1500 dimensions, so a 3" Class 900 flange is smaller than a 2-1/2".
Stud lengths are the catalogs' figures for a raised-face or ring joint; a thicker gasket or spacer needs a longer stud.
Class 400 isn't included yet: only one catalog prints it.
